brief: critic with fresh context on W1-01 province streaming pump (Engine._streamProvince from _afterStep + release hysteresis)
findings: ENVIRONMENT: the working tree at /home/user/elder-souls-claude DOES NOT BOOT. `node tools/harness/boot-check.mjs` exits 12: 'this._installTopicSupply is not a function' (engine.js:321 calls it; nothing defines it). This is a concurrent agent's in-flight edit to game/src/engine.js + game/src/character/converse.js, NOT the province work. All my measurements are therefore taken on a shadow tree pinned at HEAD=8734986 (git archive HEAD), which boot-checks PASS.
The province fix IS in HEAD 8734986: engine.js has 4 mentions of _streamProvince, province.js has the KEEP = RADIUS + 1 hysteresis. Last commit touching those two files is bd3630e.
Shadow tree needs tools/node_modules symlinked (playwright lives in tools/, not repo root).

FixedLoop.MAX_CATCHUP = 5 (game/src/core/loop.js). A 133.8 ms hitch is 8 fixed steps of arrears; the accumulator can only run 5 and then DROPS the surplus (stats.catchupDroppedMs / catchupClamps). So the builder's max frame is not merely a dropped frame, it is dropped SIMULATION TIME in play mode. Must measure catchupClamps under real rAF.

Engine.stepFrames() times only loop.stepMsTotal, accumulated by FixedLoop.stepOnce() around the STEP ALONE. _afterStep() -- and therefore _streamProvince() -- is OUTSIDE that window. So engine.perf/getPerfStats() CANNOT see the streaming cost at all. The builder correctly used its own performance.now() around stepOnce()+_afterStep() in walkTimed(); anything reading perf.simMsWindow() would report the streamer as free.

URGENT PATH IS UNBOUNDED AND COMES BEFORE THE DISC GUARD: in _streamProvince, `if (pv.queue[0].d <= STREAM_NEAR_D2) { ...pump(2); return; }` runs BEFORE `if (discWork) return;`. So a frame that just paid ~59 ms for the skin+cover rebuild can also pay 2 tile builds (~138 ms) = ~197 ms. The 'one unit of streaming work per step' claim is true only on the trickle path.

province.tileM is a dead knob: request() computes tx0/tz0 from the MODULE constant TILE_M, not this.tileM. stats() reports tileSizeM: this.tileM. Perturbing tileM would desynchronise the reported geometry from the built geometry.

Release hysteresis cannot leak by construction: KEEP is an absolute Chebyshev distance from the CURRENT focus tile, so residency is hard-bounded at (2*KEEP+1)^2 = 49. Still to measure: meshes/instances/heap growth over a long loop.

travelRide moves the body by direct position assignment at mode speed; rootspeak = 40 m/s = 0.667 m/frame. STREAM_REFOCUS_M=2 -> refocus every 3 frames; SKIN_REBUILD_M=11 -> a ~59 ms skin rebuild every ~17 frames. Must measure.

MY OWN PROBE: tools/world/critic-prov-r1.mjs (modes modality|fight|displace|loop|posed|settle|raf|ride) and tools/world/critic-prov-shot.mjs. Declared under method_deviations. Reads province.tiles/focus/discs only; never calls request/pump/drain/streamAround.

RAW PLAYER INPUT PASSES: 1500 m walked with the stick + stepFrames(1) (NOT walkRoute/walkPath), 75 checks every 600 frames, 0 samples with no ground underfoot, worst near-3x3 unbuilt 0, ring 25/25 at the end. The builder's headline reproduces on the path a real hand drives.

walkPath PASSES for residency (ends ring 25/25, underfoot true) but is itself broken: fed a 1200 m slice of the crossing spline it ran to maxFrames=400000, covered 59,873.7 m at a mean 8.98 m/s (4.5x walk speed) and never arrived, offset 686 m. Not W1-01's, but it means every walkPath-based reachability number in the tree is suspect.

SETTLE CURVE IS THE POSED-CAMERA GAP. viewpoints-province.json declares settleFrames: 24 for all 17 province viewpoints and shoot.mjs steps exactly that. From a COLD posed eye: underfoot built at frame 1, near-3x3 complete by frame 8, but the ring is only 10 of 25 at frame 24 and needs 384-512 frames (6.4-8.5 s) to close. So the builder's 'closes the shoot.mjs --direct half' is true for the 450 m the 3x3 covers and FALSE for the ring the streamer itself declares it wants: at the settle the tool actually uses, 15 of 25 tiles are missing and 15 are still queued.

POSED CAMERA DEMOLISHES THE PLAYER'S OWN WORLD. With an override eye posed 2.4 km away and a 24-frame settle, at the BODY: underfoot false, near-3x3 9 of 9 unbuilt, ring 0/25, tiles_resident 10. request() releases everything outside KEEP of the EYE. On clearing the pose the body's ground returns underfoot on frame 0, near-3x3 at frame 4, ring at frame 454. Harness-only (sim.camera.override is written only by Engine.camera()), but it is a live hazard for the pooled capture daemon's settle proof.

DEATH RESPAWN IS THE WORST FRAME IN THE BUILD, AND THE BUILDER NEVER MEASURED IT. Killed in the province after a 300 m walk: the body jumps 4142.6 m to the hearth and 1864.2 m again the next frame. The six frames after the jump cost 337.0, 405.4, 484.0, 362.0, 222.6, 472.5 ms — worst 483.96 ms, ~29 dropped frames, against the builder's walking max of 133.8 ms. Ground underfoot IS built on frame 0 and the 3x3 closes at frame 5; the ring takes 455 frames. The cost is the urgent path: pump(2) is exempt from the one-unit-per-step guard AND runs BEFORE it, so a frame pays 2 tile builds plus the skin+cover rebuild plus a ~30-tile release. (Taken at loadavg 11-15 — needs a quiet re-run.)

FIGHT (9000 frames, walking + light/heavy/roll, 4 enemies): 33 of 9000 frames did streaming work; those 33 have mean 138.4 ms, p50 142.2 ms, max 449.0 ms, 25 of 33 over 50 ms. Phases seen ROLL_STARTUP/ROLL_IFRAME/ROLL_RECOVER/ATK_STARTUP/ATK_ACTIVE/ATK_RECOVER/WALK. 17 of 1040 ROLL_IFRAME frames exceeded 16.7 ms and the worst frame in the whole run, 448.95 ms, landed INSIDE a roll's i-frame window with did=5 (ground skin + cover disc). (loadavg 13-15 — MUST re-run quiet.)

Engine.camera(pose) is the ONLY writer of sim.camera.override (engine.js 3823/3837/3873). deathCamera() uses beginDeathCamera() and sets camera.deathFrame, not override. So in play the focus is always the body — the override branch is harness-only.

FALSIFICATION PASSES — my instrument goes red on every check when Engine._streamProvince is neutered in the page (--break-fix, same walk, same tree): raw-stick 1500 m samples_with_no_ground 0 -> 25; worst near-3x3 unbuilt 0 -> 9; end ring 25/25 -> 5/25; underfoot true -> FALSE; tiles built during the walk 25 -> 0; skin/cover disc lag 9.66 m -> 1083.62 m. there-and-back leg 0 -> 28 no-ground samples. Posed eye: 25 tiles built -> 0, ring 25/25 -> 0/25. teleport-then-walk hitches over 16.7 ms 30 -> 6.

TRAVELRIDE IS THE MODALITY THE FIX DOES NOT SURVIVE. rootspeak svc-065 at 40 m/s, 3293.7 m in 4940 steps: residency is FINE (0 samples with no ground, worst near-3x3 unbuilt 0, end ring 25/25) but the cost is not — mean 8.06 ms/step, p99 212.67, p99.9 399.79, MAX 674.76 ms, 327 of 4940 steps over 16.7 ms (6.6%, vs 0.32% walking = 20x) and 273 over 50 ms (5.5%). 3293.7 m / SKIN_REBUILD_M 11 = 299 predicted skin rebuilds against 327 observed hitches: the hitch count IS the skin-rebuild count. The whole 82-second ride is one continuous stutter. (loadavg 12.5 — the RATE is robust, the absolute ms are not.)

travelRide is fare-gated at a cold start: boardTravel refuses every service with 'You have not walked the <leg> road. No one sells passage over ground you have not crossed.' I granted travel.walked for all legs to open the door (declared as a method deviation) — it opens the fare gate, it does not touch the streamer.

The builder's own AFTER-crossing.json verifies Q6: walkRoute teleports ONCE to pts[0] on (re)start and never again (engine.js:4586); the crossing artifact's speed histogram puts 33,074 of 33,078 samples in the 1.99-2.01 m/s band, walk.done true, path_m 6615.1, minutes 55.131. Genuinely walked. NOTE: the builder's status says 35 samples, the artifact's summary.samples says 34.
shoot.mjs settleFrames default is 24 (viewpoints-province.json capture block); all 17 province viewpoints inherit it and declare anchors region_* that do not exist in game/data/states.

RELEASE HYSTERESIS DOES NOT LEAK: 8 laps of a closed 1.4 km circuit, 834,176 fixed steps (3.86 simulated hours). tiles_resident flat 28-34 against a ceiling of (2*KEEP+1)^2 = 49; province meshes flat 180-230; usedJSHeapSize flat at 109,000,000; underfoot built at every lap. It DOES churn: 36-42 tile builds per lap, i.e. the same tiles destroyed and rebuilt every time round, ~2.6 s of rebuild work per lap.

rAF ACCUMULATOR: 25 s of real-time walking in mode 'play' loses 8 simulated frames with 3 catch-up clamps and 129 ms dropped, against 3 / 1 / 25.9 ms with the pump neutered (matched control, back to back, same load). Confirms the mechanism: streaming hitches become LOST SIMULATION TIME, not late frames. Applied to the respawn burst: 2,283 ms of arrears, MAX_CATCHUP 5, so ~83 ms of world advances and ~2.2 s is dropped.

province.tileM PROVED ORPHAN BY MEASUREMENT (not by reading source, which verdict-validate refuses as an artifact kind): two identical 400 m walks from a cold province, tileM 300 then 150. stats() reports tileSizeM 300 then 150; the set of built tile keys is BYTE-IDENTICAL (['5,0','5,1',...] both arms), tiles_resident 30 both. Halving the tile size must change every key floor(x/tileSize); it changed none.

RI-PLT03's S4 IS THE METRIC NOBODY COMPUTED: 'frames > 50 ms outside declared boundaries per minute of continuous walking', budget <= 1.0, fail > 3.0. My walk: 38 over 50 ms in 14,689 frames = 4.08 traversal min = 9.3/min. The builder's own attribution gives 8.7/min from the other direction. '0.32% of steps over 16.7 ms' and '9.3 hitches per traversal minute' are the same measurement and only one is in the corpus. RI-PLT03 HF4 and HF6 both trigger, capping the item at 2.

SCORING: RI-PLT03 2 (hard-fail capped), RI-MTH07 6 (4 of 5 knobs couple), RI-WLD01 traversal axis 8. Mean 5.33 -> 5. AR-1 FAIL (448.95 ms frame inside ROLL_IFRAME). AR-2 pass. AR-3 seam_sterile FALSE.

THE WORKING TREE'S BOOT BREAK WAS TRANSIENT: another agent landed _installTopicSupply mid-run and boot-check PASSES at 13:44Z. The code under test is byte-identical either way - the _streamProvince() body and the whole of game/src/world/province.js diff clean against HEAD - so every measurement describes the tree on disk now.

PICTURES: the 1500 m pair is the decisive one (with pump: a stone forest of trees, boulders and flagstones; without: a blank grey slope, underfoot_built FALSE, discs 1083.6 m behind). The 750 m pair is deliberately subtler and instructive - at 750 m the GROUND is still there, because with the pump neutered nothing ever calls request() and therefore nothing ever RELEASES either; what has gone is the ground-cover fringe. The defect arrives as missing detail before it arrives as missing ground.
notes_for_successor: BIGGEST GAP: GAP-W1-provstream-arrival-burst. The urgent branch in Engine._streamProvince (`if (pv.queue[0].d <= STREAM_NEAR_D2) { pump(STREAM_URGENT_TILES); return; }`) sits ABOVE `if (discWork) return;`, so an ARRIVAL frame pays a ~30-tile release + updateSkin(15,625 verts) + updateCover + updateNear + two _buildTile calls at once. Measured on a real death respawn: six frames of 337/405/484/362/223/472 ms. One-line fix: move the discWork guard above the urgent branch, or make the urgent budget `discWork ? 1 : STREAM_URGENT_TILES`. SECOND: skip the request() refocus while combat.player.state is ATK_*/ROLL_* - that is the AR-1 remedy and it is far cheaper than making updateSkin fast. THIRD: budget by metres-since-last-rebuild, not by frames, or travelRide at 40 m/s keeps getting a 2 m/s walk's throughput. Re-run with: node tools/world/critic-prov-r1.mjs --mode displace|ride|fight|loop|raf|settle|tilem, each with --break-fix as the falsification control. Acceptance thresholds are in the verdict's biggest_gap.remedy.acceptance. TAKE THE TIMING RUNS ON A QUIET BOX - mine were at loadavg 12-26 and the absolute milliseconds are upper bounds (the rates and the hard-fail triggers are not: S5's threshold is 100 ms and the smallest arrival-burst frame measured is 222.64 ms).
